geodesic_heat_grid — MATH geometry op

• Data kinds: image2d → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.geodesic_heat_grid(mask, source=None, *, spacing=1.0, t: 'float | None' = None) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import mathgeometry; mathgeometry.geodesic_heat_grid(mask, source=None, *, spacing=1.0, t: 'float | None' = None) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsmath.get("geodesic_heat_grid"))

Usage

Computes obstacle-avoiding geodesic distance on the grid of a 2-D image or 3-D volume by the heat method (grid version of Crane et al. 2013).

mask is a bool array (2-D or 3-D) where passable pixels/voxels are True; source is the index of the start point (1 point (i, j[, k]) or a list of points; if omitted, the first passable pixel). spacing is the pixel size per axis (scalar or per axis).

1) (I − tΔ) u = δ (spreading heat; Δ is the 2d+1-point Laplacian linking only passable pixels = obstacles are insulating)

2) X = −∇u / |∇u| (with differences across faces) 3) Solve Δφ = ∇·X and shift to 0 at the start point.

Returns {"distance", "t"} (impassable pixels, and pixels not connected to the start point, are inf).

Gate: in obstacle-free space it converges to the Euclidean distance. Pixel Dijkstra (4/8-neighbourhood) has a grid-orientation error (up to 41% with 4-neighbourhood, up to 8% with 8-neighbourhood) that does not vanish with refinement, whereas the heat method's does.

Family-wide input contract (fail-closed)

Every mathops op validates its input before computing (nothing slips through silently):

• complex input raises ValueError — coercing to float64 silently discards the imaginary part (numpy only emits a ComplexWarning and returns a plausible-looking wrong real number). State .real/.imag/abs() explicitly, or use complexops, which handles complex data.

• masked arrays with masked elements raise ValueError — the implicit conversion that peels off the mask and uses the raw values underneath is refused. Say explicitly whether to fill or to drop.

• NaN/Inf raises ValueError on every input (refused with the count stated — it propagates through the whole result).

• Shapes are strict: 1-D and 2-D are never implicitly promoted or broadcast (a matrix in a vector slot, or a vector in a matrix slot, raises ValueError; reshape explicitly).

• Size cap: ops that take a matrix, and the stat_histogram bins, raise ValueError beyond mathops.MAX_ELEMENTS (2^26 ≈ 67 million elements).
